matches.rationale: GT1 concerns inflated sample efficiency metrics in Figure 6(b) table being inconsistent with the learning curves in 6(a). Pred_id 4 identifies a different issue: the text's claimed '20-67%' range doesn't match the table's reported SE_ave/SE_peak ranges. These are distinct issues—one about table vs. curves, the other about text vs. table.

Both identify the same sign error in the f^{return} target function in Section 3.1. GT2 describes the advantage weighting sign error and its contradiction with the stated goal. Pred_id 1 explicitly identifies the negative sign in the advantage term and explains how maximizing the function would decrease (not increase) good-action probabilities, contradicting the REINFORCE claim.

GT3 concerns the failure to disclose which specific p value was used for each environment in the main results of Section 5.2. None of the findings identify this selective reporting issue about hyperparameter disclosure.

Both identify overclaiming in the abstract. GT4 notes claims of 'eliminates' and 'completely solves' are unsupported by partial improvements shown in results. Pred_id 6 identifies the same abstract claims ('completely eliminates', 'unprecedented') as unsupported by the quantitative results showing only partial improvements.

GT5 concerns fabricated or premature citations to 'Cheng et al., 2025' and 'Deng et al., 2025' in Section 6. Pred_id 2 identifies a missing 'Kumar et al. [2024]' reference in the Introduction, which is a different citation issue in a different section.

GT6 concerns the omission of ethical considerations and failure mode discussion in Section 5.3 (RLHF application) and Section 7 (Limitations). None of the findings identify this ethical integrity omission.

GT7 concerns inappropriate marketing-style rhetorical language in the Introduction ('completely solves', 'unprecedented', 'revolutionary breakthrough'). While pred_id 6 identifies overclaiming in the abstract, it does not address the rhetorical presentation manipulation in the Introduction that GT7 describes.

GT8 concerns contradiction between Section 3.1 (dynamic reference policy updated each round) and Appendix A.2 (fixed reference policy). Pred_id 7 identifies a different inconsistency about which checkpoint is used in the influence formula (θ_0 vs θ_j), not about dynamic vs. static reference policy.
GT9 concerns manipulative y-axis scaling in Figure 6(a) learning curves to visually amplify differences. None of the findings identify this visual encoding manipulation issue.

GT10 concerns asymmetric experimental design where IIF gets hyperparameter optimization (various p values) while baselines use default hyperparameters. None of the findings identify this unfair comparison issue.

GT11 concerns cherry-picking favorable interpretations despite wide confidence intervals and inconsistent performance across rounds. Pred_id 4 identifies a mismatch in reported percentage ranges but doesn't address the statistical power or cherry-picking issues GT11 describes.

Both identify inconsistency in the influence score formula in Section 3.1. GT12 notes the missing learning rate η_j and inconsistent use of θ_j. Pred_id 7 identifies the same issue: the formula uses θ_0^{(k)} but the explanation mentions θ_j^{(k)}, creating an internal inconsistency about which checkpoint is used.
GT13 concerns potential selective reporting of only successful environments while hiding failures. None of the findings identify this publication bias or negative results omission issue.

GT14 concerns misattribution of the f^{return} formulation to Sutton & Barto Section 13.4 in Section 3.1, conflating standard REINFORCE with the paper's novel construction. None of the findings identify this specific reference misattribution issue.

GT15 concerns contradiction between Section 5.1's claim of 'negligible overhead' and Table 5/Section 5.3 showing influence calculation as a substantial cost (7-15% in RL, exceeding forward passes in RLHF). None of the findings identify this specific computational cost contradiction.
